title: Nine Storms and One Loose Tile
subtitle: 灾害损失 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 灾害损失（灾害防范·灾害损失与修复）
meta: 主题语境：灾害损失（灾害防范·灾害损失与修复）　|　核心词汇：damage　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 damage 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the surveyor ① assessed a damage that no insurer in the county would have admitted, and he said the assessing was the whole of the repair. The ② damage, meaning the harm and not the cost, ran nine storms and stayed unrepaired on the roof; damage, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left open.

Every ③ damage in that street had the same loose tile above it, and the ④ damage at the end, meaning the one they left for the winter and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever claimed twice. Damage, the builder said, is nine parts water and one part somebody willing to climb; the surveyor said the climbing is the part that fills nine storms.

The accountant meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the damage was the whole of the claim, meaning the money and not the harm. The ⑥ damage, meaning the money and not any of that, is the only thing in a claim that everybody totals and nobody repairs; damage, he said, is either something you assess or the only word that means both a harm and a money. He said the money is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ damage had become a line in a policy, and the policy had become an argument about the loose tile. The ⑧ damage of the whole thing, the surveyor wrote in December, was one street and nine storms of climbing; damage, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to climb. She said the climbing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ damage I remember is the one at the end, which was settled in 1978 and is still described as the oldest in the street. A ⑩ damage, the builder said in 1980, is the only thing that improves by being repaired; every damage, she said, is a money that has agreed to look like a harm. She said the money was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 损坏；损毁（指房子或街上出现的那一处）
B. n. 损坏（指那种损害本身，与那笔费用相对）
C. 固定搭配：assess a damage 评估一处损坏
D. n. 损坏（指留到冬天才修的那一处）
E. n. 损坏；损害（抽象总称，指一条街上累积的破损）
F. n. 损失（指保单里写到、被列明的那一笔）
G. n. 损害赔偿金（指索赔中结算的那笔钱）
H. n. 赔偿金（抽象总称，指人人合计却无人去修的那笔）

items.q: assessed a damage that no insurer in the county would have admitted
The damage, meaning the harm and not the cost
the damage was the whole of the claim
the damage had become a line in a policy
The damage of the whole thing
A damage, the builder said in 1980

answers.why: assess a damage 意为“评估一处损坏”，1954 年勘测员评估了一处全县没有一家保险公司肯承认的损坏。
damage 意为“损坏”，指那种损害本身而不是那笔费用，它在屋顶上历经九场风暴而从未修。
damage 意为“损坏”，指那条街上每一处损坏，每一处上方都有同一块松动的瓦。
damage 意为“损坏”，指留到冬天才修的那一处，是唯一有人索赔过两次的。
damage 意为“损害赔偿金”，指索赔中结算的那笔钱，会计说这笔赔偿金就是那次索赔的全部。
damage 意为“赔偿金”，指人人合计却无人去修的那笔钱而不是别的，是索赔里人人都合计、却无人去修补的东西。
damage 意为“损失”，指保单里写到、被列明的那一笔，到 1962 年这笔损失成了保单里的一行。
damage 意为“损坏、损害”，勘测员十二月写道，整件事的损害是一条街和九场风暴的攀爬检修。
damage 意为“损害赔偿金”，我记得的是末尾那一笔，1978 年结清，至今仍被说成街上最久的一笔。
damage 为抽象总称，施工者 1980 年说，一处损坏是唯一会因为被修好而变得更好的东西。
